overview: HASEKO Corporation is Japan's largest condominium ("mansion") contractor and developer, with a cumulative total of roughly 640,000+ condominium units built since constructing its first in 1968. The group operates across four segments -- Construction-Related (condominium design/build, detached housing, non-residential), Real Estate-Related (for-sale condominium development, land trading, income property), Condominium Management and Operation (building management, leasing, renovation/resale, senior housing), and Overseas (Hawaii mixed-use development, US mainland rental apartments) -- and is headquartered in Tokyo with fiscal year ending March 31.

business_model.summary: Haseko earns the majority of profit from non-consolidated construction contracts for condominiums (often exclusive, construction-with-design orders from developer clients including its own real estate subsidiaries), supplemented by real estate sales (its own for-sale condominium and land development business) and a growing, more annuity-like condominium management/operation business (building management, leasing agency, renovation resale, senior housing). FY2025 consolidated net sales were JPY1,273.1bn: Completed construction contracts ~49% (JPY625.2bn), Real estate sales ~40% (JPY511.1bn), Leasing & management ~8% (JPY98.1bn), Design & supervision ~1% (JPY15.7bn), Other ~2%. By segment, Construction-Related Business was JPY900.9bn of segment sales (incl. intercompany), Real Estate-Related JPY293.2bn, Condominium Management and Operation JPY165.4bn, and Overseas JPY4.3bn (loss-making).

revenue_streams.name: Real estate sales (for-sale condominiums, land, income property)
Other businesses (renovation, brokerage, senior housing, overseas)

business_model.customer_type: Primarily B2B: condominium developers/project owners (including Haseko's own real estate subsidiaries), landowners, rental/company-housing sponsors, plus B2C end-buyers of for-sale condominiums and homeowners via renovation/management services
business_model.geographic_mix: Overwhelmingly domestic Japan (Tokyo metropolitan area ~51% of condominium management units, Kansai ~34%, with construction orders concentrated in Tokyo metro ~79% and Kansai/Tokai regions); small and currently loss-making overseas exposure in Hawaii (Ewa mixed-use project on Oahu) and US mainland rental apartment development, together only ~0.3% of FY2025 net sales

main_competitors: general contractors (Shimizu, Obayashi, Taisei) for large-scale builds
competitive_position.market_position: Self-described leading condominium contractor in Japan by cumulative units built (~640,000+ since 1968); non-consolidated orders received reached a record JPY726.7bn in FY2025 (up 23.9% YoY), a record high for the third consecutive year, with exclusive-contract orders running ~90-95% of private-sector condominium orders and construction-with-design orders also at a high level -- indicating deep, sticky relationships with developer clients rather than competitive general-contractor bidding

moat_factors.factor: Scale and specialization in condominium construction
moat_factors.description: Decades of focus on condominium design-build gives cost, scheduling and land-sourcing (land for orders) advantages versus generalist contractors; high share of exclusive and design-build contracts (~90%+) reduces competitive bidding pressure

In-house real estate development, construction, sales, and post-sale building/rental management creates a recurring revenue tail (condominium management covers 453,500+ units) and cross-sell into renovation and resale of condos it originally built
Ability to source land and provide planning/design services ahead of construction orders builds switching costs for repeat developer clients
Long operating history (founded 1937, condominiums since 1968) and large installed base support trust among condominium associations awarding management contracts

weaknesses: Heavy single-country, single-product concentration in Japanese condominiums, directly exposed to Tokyo/Kansai property cycles and new-supply trends (Tokyo new condo supply fell to lowest since 1973 in 2025)
Overseas diversification (Hawaii, US mainland) has been consistently loss-making for several years, diluting otherwise strong domestic returns
Construction margins have historically been volatile and sensitive to input cost and labor cost inflation, which the company does not fully control

Recent JFTC antimonopoly investigations into subsidiary Haseko Reform (repair/renovation order bid-rigging, both Kanto and Tokai regions) pose reputational and potential penalty risk in a business segment built on trust with condominium associations

growth_drivers: Record non-consolidated orders received for four consecutive fiscal years (FY2026 forecast JPY730.0bn), providing revenue visibility via a large construction backlog (JPY940.0bn total completed-construction-revenue backlog forecast for FY2026, up from JPY788.4bn in FY2025)

Construction gross margin recovery -- profit ratio of completed construction contracts rose from 12.5% (FY2024) to 14.1% (FY2025) and is guided to 15.9% for FY2026, a major driver of the 'HASEKO Evolution Plan' profit growth
New precast concrete (PCa) plant commenced operations to build a more sustainable, less labor-dependent production system amid Japan's construction labor shortage
Expansion into non-residential construction (e.g., large-scale data center order) and rental condominium/company housing orders, diversifying beyond pure private-sector condominiums
Real estate business turning over assets faster (turnover ratios improving across for-sale condominium, income property and renovation categories) to improve capital efficiency and ROE
Condominium management and operation business steadily growing unit counts (453,500 units managed, up from 448,076) providing a recurring, less cyclical earnings stream

Shift to a 'light-asset' overseas model -- April 2026 acquisition of a 30% stake in a US rental-apartment developer/builder, aiming for earnings recovery accelerating from FY2027 while reducing balance-sheet risk versus direct Hawaii-style development

Capital efficiency initiatives: JPY20.0bn treasury share buyback in FY2025, progressive dividend policy (DPS raised from JPY85 to JPY95 to a planned JPY100 for FY2026), and a medium-term target of total shareholder return ratio of ~50% of profit over the FY2025-FY2030 plan period

Medium-term 'HASEKO Evolution Plan' (FY2025-FY2030) targeting consolidated ordinary profit of JPY100bn+ and ROE sustained above 10%, reaching ~13% by FY2030 -- FY2025 ordinary profit of JPY94.1bn already exceeded initial plan forecasts, and FY2026 guidance of JPY105bn would mark the first time above JPY100bn since FY2019

business.description: Revenue and margins are tied to private-sector condominium order volume and pricing in Tokyo metro/Kansai; any downturn in condo demand, affordability or new-supply economics would hit both construction orders and real estate sale margins

Hawaii (Ewa project) and US mainland operations have posted ordinary losses for multiple years (JPY-7.7bn in FY2025, guided JPY-3.4bn in FY2026); inventory valuation losses (JPY4.1bn in FY2025 related to planned Hawaii hotel land sale) show execution risk in unfamiliar overseas markets
Reliance on a relatively small number of large developer clients and land/project owners for big-ticket orders (e.g., single projects of 600-1,000 units) creates lumpiness in quarterly order intake

Subsidiary Haseko Reform has been subject to on-site JFTC inspections in both the Kanto (Mar 2025) and Tokai (Jul 2026) regions over alleged bid-rigging in condominium large-scale repair orders; potential cease-and-desist orders, fines, and reputational damage to a segment dependent on condominium-association trust

financial.risk: Interest-bearing debt and rising Japanese rates
financial.description: Interest-bearing debt of ~JPY418.5-425.0bn (D/E ratio ~0.73-0.76x) funds land banking and real estate inventory; a shift away from Japan's ultra-low rate environment raises financing costs and could pressure real estate segment margins and overseas investment returns

Large real estate and overseas investment balance (JPY819.7-831.7bn) is sensitive to land price corrections or project-level impairments, as seen in the FY2025 extraordinary losses (~JPY4.6bn, including impairments) and the FY2024 larger impairment charge (~JPY16.9bn)

Operating cash flow swung from roughly breakeven/negative in several recent years (e.g., FY2024 non-consolidated OCF negative) to a strong JPY157.4bn in FY2025, reflecting lumpy inventory and deposit timing inherent to condominium development accounting

regulatory.description: Ongoing JFTC investigations into renovation/repair order bid-rigging could result in administrative orders, fines and mandated compliance remediation, and may affect Haseko Reform's ability to win large-scale repair contracts going forward
Japan's April 2024 overtime cap on construction workers (part of the 'work-style reform') is cited across the industry as adding 5-10% to labor costs and limiting construction capacity/scheduling
Changes to building codes, condominium management legislation, or real estate transaction/property taxes in Japan could affect demand or compliance costs

macro.risk: Construction material and labor cost inflation
macro.description: Industry-wide construction cost inflation (estimated ~5% annually through 2026-2027) driven by material price volatility and chronic skilled-labor shortages directly pressures Haseko's completed-construction gross margins, which only recently recovered from FY2024 lows

As the Bank of Japan normalizes policy rates, higher mortgage rates could dampen condominium buyer demand/affordability, while also raising Haseko's own funding costs for land banking and real estate inventory

Japan's shrinking and aging population is a structural long-term constraint on new housing demand, though it is partially offset by continued urban concentration in Tokyo/Osaka and growing demand for condominium management, renovation and senior housing services serving an aging, urbanizing population

macro.risk: Record-low new condo supply / affordability ceiling
macro.description: Tokyo's new condominium supply fell to its lowest level since 1973 in 2025 amid rapidly rising prices (average new condo price in central Tokyo's 23 wards up ~21.8% in 2025 to ~JPY136 million); further price escalation risks pricing out buyers and slowing unit absorption, even as it supports Haseko's per-unit construction/sale economics in the near term

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Japanese condominium construction cost inflation is forecast at roughly 5% annually through 2026-2027 before easing, driven by labor shortages and material costs; Tokyo new condo supply hit a 50+ year low in 2025 but is forecast to recover modestly (~+4.7%) in 2026, with prices at record highs, reflecting a structurally tight supply/high-price environment that favors established, scaled contractors like Haseko able to pass through costs and secure land
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate-to-high -- construction order intake and real estate sales/margins are sensitive to Japan's property cycle, land prices, and interest rates, though the growing condominium management/operation business (recurring building management, leasing) provides a partial, more stable offset
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate -- rising Japanese interest rates raise Haseko's own financing costs on ~JPY420bn of interest-bearing debt and large real estate inventory, and could soften end-buyer mortgage affordability; the company's financial income/expense line swung further negative (JPY-4.5bn in FY2025 from JPY-1.6bn in FY2024) reflecting this pressure

recent_developments.event: Analyst consensus on Investing.com shows a 'Buy' rating (5 buy/2 hold/1 sell among 8 analysts) with an average 12-month price target around JPY3,250, following a Nomura upgrade to Buy (JPY3,490 target) in May 2026; shares have traded in a roughly JPY2,450-3,530 range over the trailing year

Q1 FY2026 (June quarter) results released: consolidated net sales JPY312.1bn (+9.2% YoY), ordinary profit JPY30.5bn (+58.9% YoY), driven by a sharp construction gross margin improvement (completed-construction profit ratio 17.7% vs 13.2% prior-year 1Q) and high-value for-sale condominium deliveries; non-consolidated orders received surged 93.8% YoY to JPY248.8bn

JFTC opened a second bid-rigging investigation (Tokai region: Aichi, Gifu, Mie) into more than 20 condominium repair firms including subsidiary Haseko Reform, separate from the earlier March 2025 Kanto-region inspection; Haseko stated the subsidiary is cooperating fully
Haseko disclosed that Haseko Reform remains under ongoing JFTC investigation following media reports of possible administrative action related to large-scale condominium repair order bid-rigging

FY2025 (year ended March 2026) full results: record consolidated net sales of JPY1,273.1bn (+8.1% YoY), operating profit JPY98.7bn (+16.6%), ordinary profit JPY94.1bn (+12.8%), net profit JPY54.8bn (+59.2%, aided by absence of the prior year's large extraordinary impairment losses); non-consolidated orders received hit a record JPY726.7bn (+23.9% YoY); FY2026 guidance set at net sales JPY1,380.0bn (+8.4%) and record ordinary profit of JPY105.0bn (+11.6%), with ROE guided to 11.3%

Board proposed raising the FY2025 year-end dividend by JPY5 to JPY50 (annual DPS JPY95, payout ratio 46.4%, total shareholder return including buybacks 83.3%), and guided FY2026 annual DPS to JPY100 (+JPY5 YoY)

Haseko North America acquired a 30% stake in a US real estate developer/builder focused on rental apartment development and construction, part of a strategic shift to a lighter-asset overseas model to diversify risk and improve capital efficiency
First year of the 'HASEKO Evolution Plan' (FY2025-FY2030) executed broadly as planned, with the Group purchasing JPY20.0bn of treasury shares during the year to improve ROE and capital efficiency

guidance.management_commentary: Management characterized FY2025 as 'a year of steady progress' toward a medium-term target of JPY100bn consolidated ordinary profit, noting the JPY94.1bn FY2025 result exceeded initial forecasts and FY2026 guidance of JPY105bn would reach the plan's profit target roughly a year ahead of schedule. Management flagged construction margin recovery, record order backlog, and continued ROE-focused capital allocation (treasury buybacks, progressive dividends) as the core 2026 priorities, while explicitly stating that the impact of Middle East geopolitical tensions on orders and construction activity is 'currently considered to be limited.' Overseas commentary emphasized a deliberate shift toward a lighter-asset, equity-method model in the US to reduce balance-sheet risk after years of Hawaii-related losses.

bull_case: Record order backlog (JPY940.0bn of forecast completed-construction revenue) and four consecutive years of record non-consolidated orders provide strong multi-year revenue visibility
Construction gross margins are recovering sharply (12.5% to 14.1% to a guided 15.9%), directly driving operating leverage and record ordinary profit guidance of JPY105bn for FY2026

Shareholder-friendly capital allocation: progressive dividend (JPY85 to JPY95 to a guided JPY100), JPY20bn treasury buyback in FY2025, and a medium-term target of ~50% total shareholder return of profit

Trades at a modest valuation (P/E ~11x, per info.json screen data) despite record profits, a sub-1x D/E of ~0.73x, and improving ROE (10.0% actual FY2025, guided 11.3% FY2026, targeting ~13% by FY2030), leaving room for re-rating if execution continues

Diversification into recurring condominium management/leasing (453,500+ units managed) and a strategic pivot to a capital-light overseas model reduce reliance on volatile new-construction order cycles
bear_case: Heavy concentration in Japanese condominium construction and real estate leaves the company exposed to a cyclical downturn, record-low new supply, or an affordability ceiling after years of sharp price increases (Tokyo new condo prices +21.8% in 2025 alone)

Ongoing JFTC antimonopoly investigations into subsidiary Haseko Reform across two regions (Kanto and Tokai) create uncertainty around potential fines, cease-and-desist orders, and reputational damage in a trust-dependent business

Industry-wide construction cost and labor inflation (~5%/year) could erode the recently recovered construction margins if cost pass-through to clients proves harder than assumed in the 15.9% FY2026 target

Overseas business remains structurally loss-making (Hawaii Ewa project, prior inventory valuation losses) and the newly announced light-asset US pivot is unproven, adding execution risk without yet contributing meaningfully to profit

Rising Japanese interest rates increase financing costs on a large, debt-funded real estate inventory/land bank (~JPY420bn of interest-bearing debt) and could simultaneously weaken end-buyer mortgage affordability, squeezing the business from both sides
